# Estimation

Recall that the differenced model is
$\Delta Y=\Delta\vdagger+\Delta Z'\theta_\dagger+\Delta U$, with $\vdagger$ the
unknown function and $W$ taking values in $\{0,1,\dots,\mathsf L-1\}$. We estimate
$\vdagger$ in a $\varphi$-step, which
solves an ill-posed inverse problem by regularisation and returns a rate slower
than $n^{-1/2}$; the $\theta$-step is a cross-fitted one-step on a moment built to
be insensitive to that error to first order. The multinomial first stage fits the
$\mathsf L-1$ propensities $\varrho_1,\dots,\varrho_{\mathsf L-1}$, which is why
A0 asks that $\mathsf L$ be known: the analyst has to know how many functions to
fit. A4(i)'s overlap floor $\varepsilon_\varrho$ lies in $(0,1/\mathsf L)$ and is
imposed at every cell including the base one, so it tightens mechanically as cells
are added, and \eqref{eq:omegafloor} converts it into
$\lambda_{\min}(\Omega(\Delta Z))\ge\varepsilon_\varrho/\mathsf L$.

What keeps the two from being circular is an anchor, and the anchor is licensed by
\S2 rather than assumed.

One requirement of the assumption block is a restriction on how the analyst writes
$\Delta Z$, and it is stated here because it is invisible where it is imposed.
A4(ii) asks that the number $d_Z$ of non-degenerate coordinates of $\Delta Z$
satisfy $1\le d_Z\le p-1$, degenerate meaning almost surely equal to a constant.
Read against A1b(iv) the upper bound is sharper than it looks. It says at least one
coordinate of $\Delta Z$ is almost surely constant; that constant cannot be zero,
since a zero coordinate makes a row and a column of $E[\Delta Z\Delta Z']$ vanish
and A1b(iv) fails; and there cannot be two of them, since two non-zero constant
coordinates make two rows of that matrix proportional and A1b(iv) fails again. So
the two clauses together force $d_Z=p-1$ exactly, and force $\Delta Z$ to carry
exactly one constant coordinate, non-zero: *the differenced equation must include a
period effect.* What is not required is that the period effect be non-zero in the
population, its coefficient being an ordinary component of $\theta_\dagger$ that
may be zero; what is required is that the coordinate be present, so that
$\Delta Z$ spans an intercept in differences. A specification in which every
coordinate of $\Delta Z$ varies is excluded by A4(ii), and one in which two do not
is excluded by A1b(iv).

The lower bound does different work and is not a modelling choice. At $d_Z=0$ the
propensity exponent $\alpha=r/(2r+d_Z)$ is $\tfrac12$ exactly, A5(i)'s declared
floor puts $\hat\delta_n$ at $n^{-1/2}\sqrt{\ln n}$, and the sieve-entropy
condition $L_x\ln n=o(n\hat\delta_n^{2})$ then reads $L_x=o(1)$, which no integer
$L_x\ge1$ satisfies. \Cref{prp:phirate} has no admissible sieve dimension there and
\cref{thm:rootn} is vacuous rather than false. That is not a pathology of the
propensity, which at $d_Z=0$ is a constant and estimable at the parametric rate;
what fails is the $\varphi$-step's entropy budget, which needs room between the
noise level and the sieve dimension.

The $\varphi$-step is iterated linearisation with sieve Landweber--Fridman
(\cref{def:lfstep}). At stage $k$ we pose the linear equation
$\hat{\mathcal A}_{\hat\varphi^{(k-1)}}v=-\hat T_{h_x}(\hat\varphi^{(k-1)},\theta)$
on the spline sieve $\mathcal S_n$ of A8 \citep[see][]{devorelorentz1993,schumaker2007},
solve it by Landweber--Fridman from $v_0=0$ at the relaxation
\eqref{eq:normconst} \citep[see][]{dunker2014,engl2000}, and add the update to the
previous iterate.

*Every Landweber pass is applied to a linear equation*; the nonlinearity is carried
by the outer index $k$ and by nothing else. That is what makes a tangential cone
condition \citep{hanke1995} unnecessary, and the point is stronger than
convenience. The cone condition is not merely strong here: the supplement refutes
it, proving that its event has probability zero, and proving that for every
bounded candidate linearisation and for the one unbounded candidate as well.

The refutation is bounded, and the three qualifiers are load-bearing: the
condition is posed on $\mathcal V$, in the levels parameterisation, off the sieve.
A cone condition restricted to $\mathcal S_n$ is untouched by the refutation and is
also unproved, as part (3) of the supplement's remark on where the failure stops
records, and in a space of derivatives the proposition
dissolves altogether at a cost in the source index \eqref{eq:muhalf} will not pay.
Nothing in the argument above needs any of that: the $\varphi$-step is licensed by
the linearity of each pass, not by the refutation.

The derivative parameterisation is available and we decline it. Estimating the
derivative of the structural function is standard in the linear problem and
carries into the nonlinear one, where it lifts a saturation ceiling on the source
index \citep{florens2012,centorrinofeveflorens2019}. Here it pushes the wrong
way. Composing with the inverse derivative operator raises the degree of
ill-posedness from $a$ to $a+1$ *and* lowers the source index from $s/(2a)$ to
$(s-1)/\{2(a+1)\}$. At the frontier-clearing configuration $(s,a)=(3,\tfrac34)$
of the Monte Carlo that returns $\tfrac47$ in place of $2$, below the $\tfrac56$ that
\eqref{eq:muhalf} requires.

We leave recovering marginal effects from $\hat\varphi$ to future research.

We stop the iteration on a discrepancy principle at a level that is
stage-dependent and deterministic, and both features are load-bearing.

Stage-dependent, because the data error of the stage-$k$ equation is not
$\hat\delta_n$ but $\hat\delta_n\ln n$ plus the linearisation remainder
$h_u^{-2}\varepsilon_{k-1}^{2}$. A fixed level sits below the true data error in
exactly the regime the recursion must pass through, and there the classical
discrepancy guarantee does not apply.

Deterministic, for two reasons of different status. The first is this paper's own
and is sharp: the realised residual cannot supply the level, because bounding the
unobservable error from below through the residual would require a lower bound on
$\|\hat{\mathcal A}v\|$ in terms of $\|v\|$. That
$\|\hat{\mathcal A}v_\dagger\|\ll\|v_\dagger\|$ is available is not an accident of
this construction but the definition of ill-posedness. The second is classical and
is cited: no rule depending on the data alone can make a regularisation method
convergent for a genuinely ill-posed problem \citep{bakushinskii1984}.

*That statement is weaker than it looks here.* It is worst-case and deterministic,
and in the statistical setting we inhabit it does not exclude data-driven
selection. Lepskii-type balancing over the regularisation index is purely
data-driven and attains the optimal rate up to a logarithmic factor
\citep[see][]{dunker2021,lepskii1990}. We therefore prefer the schedule of
\eqref{eq:lfsched}, and are not forced into it.

It is preferred at a stated price. That schedule is *computable* from four inputs, and it
is not *known*: the two constants $\mathsf c_{14}$ and $\mathsf c_{15}$ must be chosen and
are not identified by the data, and what they must dominate are analytic constants built
from the kernel, from the design, and from the spectral pre-image radius
$\mathsf R_\ast$ of (P-a.3).

The error is not symmetric in direction. Chosen too large, the rule stops
earlier, the rate is unchanged in order and the constant degrades. Chosen too
small, the implemented level again sits below the true data error at some stage and
the discrepancy guarantee is void, leaving whatever the cap \eqref{eq:cap} returns.
This is the one place the procedure carries a tuning constant the theory does not
pin, and we say so here rather than leave it to be discovered.

\Cref{prp:phirate} is the rate: $\|\hat\varphi-\vdagger\|_{L^{2}(\pi)}=O_P(\delta_n)$ with
$\delta_n=(\hat\delta_n\ln n)^{2\mu/(2\mu+1)}$, at a finite $\bar k$ that does not grow
with $n$, and $\delta_n=o_P(n^{-1/4})$ whenever the frontier \eqref{eq:frontier} holds. It
discharges A5(i)--(iii) rather than assuming them. Two things we do not claim
should be read with it. It is an upper bound and not a
sharpness statement, and nothing there says $\delta_n$ cannot be improved. And the
source index $\mu$ is *primitive*, at (P-a.3), together with $\mathsf R_\ast$.

H1 fixes the Sobolev scale and supplies A2's Picard form, but the identity
$\mu=s/(2a)$ is not used on the rate route. The passage from a Hilbert-scale source
condition plus a link condition to the *spectral* condition the classical
discrepancy theorem consumes is operator interpolation at exponent $2\mu$. That is
available only at $2\mu\le1$, while \eqref{eq:muhalf} forces $2\mu>\tfrac53$. A
referee who asks what pins $\mu$ should be given that answer and not the identity.

The $\theta$-step runs on the debiased moment $\psi$ of \eqref{eq:psidef}: the differenced
least-squares moment plus $\widetilde W$ times a weight evaluated at the residual.
We split the observations into $\mathsf F$ folds fixed independently of the data
(\cref{def:crossfit}), compute every nuisance on the complement of the fold it is
evaluated on, and take the one-step \eqref{eq:onestep} from the plug-in
preliminary \eqref{eq:prelimtheta} \citep[see][]{chernozhukov2018dml,neweyrobins2018}.

The preliminary inherits the first-stage rate,
$\|\hat\theta^{(0)}-\theta_\dagger\|=O_P(n^{-1/2})+O_P(\delta_n)$, and it inherits it
because $\theta_\dagger$ is identified by restriction (B) alone (the plug-in
preliminary lemma of the supplement); no condition on the weight, on the propensity or on A2 enters it. Its variance estimator
is the sample sandwich \eqref{eq:Sighat}, which carries a transpose because $\hat J$ is
not symmetric even though $J$ is.

We run the $\varphi$-step at a fixed anchor $\theta_\circ$ chosen in advance of
the data, and that is what removes the circularity.

It is licensed and not free. By \cref{cor:opsol} and \cref{lem:shiftinv} the
population solution set of the operator equation in $\varphi$ is $\mathcal V_{CI}$
at *every* $\theta$, so under A1b(iii) the $\varphi$-step targets $\vdagger$ at
$\theta_\circ$ as well as at $\theta_\dagger$. What is not $\theta$-free is the
conditioning of the inverse problem. In
\eqref{eq:Adef} a conditional density is evaluated at a $\theta$-dependent point,
so the singular values, the degree of ill-posedness $a$, the source index $\mu$,
the radius $\mathsf R_\ast$ and the operator noise $\hat\delta_n$ are all
$\theta_\circ$-specific, and \cref{prp:phirate}'s hypotheses are read there. The
population solution set is $\theta$-free; the operator is not.

Debiasing enters through the choice of weight, and \cref{prp:orthog} prices all three
nuisance directions. In the structural direction the derivative of the moment vanishes for
every $h\in\mathcal V$ if and only if the representer solves the adjoint equation
$\mathcal A^\ast_{\mathrm{cond}}\ell^\Pi=-\nu/\pi$, which is A2. In the weight direction it
vanishes *exactly*, at every perturbation and not merely to first order, because $\psi$ is
bi-affine there.

In the propensity direction it vanishes exactly if and only if the weight satisfies
N1, conditional centring given $\Delta Z$. N1 can always be arranged by a
straightforward re-anchoring, at no cost to $\partial_uL$ and none to $E[\psi]$, but it does not
hold automatically, and \cref{prp:orthog}(iii) is the statement of exactly what its
failure costs. That equivalence is what demotes $\varrho$ from a $\sqrt n$ nuisance
to a product-rate one. Forming the weight never requires a weighting measure on
$\mathcal T$ to be chosen:
by Lemma L-2 of the supplement the estimator solves for $L$ inside a dense class,
so we compute no $t$-integral in forming it, which is also the argument against a
continuum-GMM formulation \citep{carrascoflorens2000}.

*We assume two ingredients of this estimator to exist with stated properties and
construct neither in this paper; three further conditions we take as primitive
rather than derive. Each is named in a hypothesis rather than buried in a
regularity condition.*

The two unbuilt ingredients are estimators. The estimator $\hat\ell$ of the
representer is priced by A5(iv) at rate $\epsilon_n$ with
$\delta_n\epsilon_n=o_P(n^{-1/2})$, and no construction attaining that rate is
supplied. The preliminary $\hat\varphi^{(0)}$ has no supplier either, the schedule
\eqref{eq:lfsched} needing it at a declared deterministic envelope
$\hat\varepsilon_0$ of polynomial order, for which consistency will not do.

The three primitives are conditions, not objects. Both $\mu$ and $\mathsf R_\ast$
are primitive, as above. Global identification of $\vdagger$ is assumed at
A1b(iii) and not derived. And on the sieve branch of the first-order bias, the
sieve display of Lemma L-7 in the supplement is assumed.

Obligations of a second kind are construction claims rather than assumptions and
are carried explicitly by the hypotheses that consume them. The first is that
$\hat L^{(-k)}$ *is* an anchored antiderivative
$L^{\,\hat b^{(-k)}}_{\hat\ell^{(-k)}}$ of a bounded, $u$-continuous
$\hat\ell^{(-k)}$, which is (R-a) of \cref{thm:rootn}. The second is that the
direction $\hat L^{(-k)}-L_\star$ is conditionally centred, which is (R-c), a
disjunction whose first branch assumes N1$'$ and whose second *prices the failure*
at $r_n\epsilon^{L}_n$ through the fourth term of the supplement's bias
decomposition. Pricing a failure is the honest third option, and it is neither a
discharge nor an evasion. The supplement's remark on open verification obligations
is the single inventory.
